summary_zh: 韩国殉道者的声音（Voice of Martyrs Korea，以下简称韩国VOM）正在开展一项事工，向9个国家因信仰而遭受迫害的基督徒家庭的儿童送去圣诞礼物盒。韩国VOM近日宣布，计划向尼日利亚、尼泊尔、埃塞俄比亚、喀麦隆、加沙地带和约旦河西岸、印度、菲律宾、布基纳法索等国家和地区受迫害的基督徒家庭的儿童提供圣诞礼物盒。继去年之后，今年也将继续以相同的地区为中心开展该项事工。玄淑·波利代表表示：“去年，在众多捐助者的鼎力相助下，我们得以送出900多份圣诞礼物盒。然而，这些地区仍有许多儿童去年未能收到礼物，因此今年我们计划继续以这些地区为重点，分发礼物盒。” 礼盒中包括儿童圣经、基督教故事书、文具以及食品和衣物等。
title_zh: 为9个受迫害国家基督教家庭的孩子们送上圣诞礼物盒
content:
한국순교자의소리(Voice of Martyrs Korea, 이하 한국VOM)가 신앙 때문에 핍박받는 9개국 기독교인 가정의 어린이들에게 성탄절 선물 상자를 전달하는 사역을 진행한다.

한국VOM은 최근 나이지리아와 네팔, 에티오피아, 카메룬, 가자지구와 요르단강 서안지구, 인도, 필리핀, 부르키나파소 등에서 핍박받는 기독교인 가정의 어린이들을 대상으로 성탄절 선물 상자를 지원할 계획이라고 밝혔다. 지난해에 이어 올해도 같은 지역을 중심으로 사역을 이어갈 예정이다.

현숙 폴리 대표는 “지난해 많은 후원자의 동역으로 900개가 넘는 성탄절 선물 상자를 전달할 수 있었다”며 “그러나 지난해 선물을 받지 못한 어린이들이 해당 지역에 여전히 많이 남아 있어 올해에도 같은 지역을 중심으로 선물 상자를 배포할 계획”이라고 밝혔다.

선물 상자에는 어린이 성경과 기독교 이야기책, 학용품을 비롯해 식료품과 의류, 장난감, 위생용품 등 생활에 필요한 물품이 담긴다. 상자 하나를 준비하는 데 드는 비용은 5만 원이며, 물품은 한국에서 일괄적으로 보내는 방식이 아니라 순교자의 소리 현지 사역자들이 각 지역에서 직접 조달해 전달한다.

현지 교회들도 사역의 중요한 역할을 담당한다. 지원이 필요한 어린이와 가정을 파악하고 선물 배포를 계획하며, 성탄절 이후에도 해당 가정과 관계를 이어가며 돌봄을 제공한다. 일부 선물 상자는 비기독교인 가정 어린이들을 위한 전도 사역에도 활용될 예정이다.

폴리 현숙 대표는 선물 상자가 물품 이상의 의미를 전한다고 설명했다. 그녀는 “우리가 전하는 옷은 결국 해지고, 음식은 다 소비되고, 학용품도 사용하다 보면 모두 없어지겠지만, 각각의 성탄절 선물 상자를 통해 전해지는 메시지는 훨씬 더 오래 남을 것”이라며 “아이들은 자신들이 하나님께 사랑받고 있으며, 전 세계 기독교인과 한 몸 된 믿음의 공동체에 속해 있고, 하나님 나라의 백성들이 자신들을 기억하고 있다는 메시지를 받게 될 것”이라고 말했다.

지난해 각 지역에서 진행된 사역은 어린이들의 구체적인 필요에 맞춰 이뤄졌다.

나이지리아 북부에서는 순교자의소리가 지원하는 위기돌봄센터(Crisis Care Home)에서 지내는 어린이 87명이 가족이나 친척과 함께 성탄절을 보내기 어려운 상황에 놓여 있었다. 이들 가운데 상당수는 테러와 관련된 비극으로 부모를 잃거나 거주지를 떠난 어린이들이었다. 일부 어린이는 핍박받는 여성과 자녀들을 위한 쉼터에서 어머니와 함께 생활하고 있었다. 어린이들은 새 옷과 신발, 성탄절 특별 식사와 간식, 운동용품과 공예 재료 등을 선물 받았다.

네팔에서는 서부의 외딴 지역을 포함한 여러 지역에서 어린이 360명에게 선물 상자가 전달됐다. 방한복과 털모자, 양말, 목도리 등 겨울철 의류와 함께 책가방, 필기구, 채색 도구, 계산기, 컴퍼스와 각도기 등이 제공됐다. 칫솔과 치약, 비누 등 위생용품과 어린이 성경, 기독교 이야기책도 상자에 담겼다.

에티오피아 티그레이 지역에서는 복음주의 교회 소속 어린이 143명이 선물을 받았다. 현지 교회 지도자들은 도움이 필요한 어린이들을 파악하고 성탄절 주간에 가족들이 함께 모일 수 있도록 지원했다. 선물 상자에는 밀가루와 쌀, 식용유, 비누, 기독교 아동 도서 등이 포함됐다. 한 어머니는 “우리 아이들은 생전 처음 성탄절 선물을 받았다”고 전했다.

카메룬에서는 핍박과 강제 이주, 경제적 어려움을 겪는 분쟁 지역 기독교 가정의 어린이들을 지원했다. 현지 사역팀은 성탄절 수개월 전부터 각 가정과 목회자, 청년 지도자들을 만나 어린이들의 필요를 파악하고 연령과 상황에 맞는 선물 상자를 준비했다. 현지 교회들은 예배와 게임, 어린이 발표, 공동체 식사 등을 마련해 함께 성탄절을 기념했다.

가자지구에서는 어린이 146명, 가자지구 출신으로 요르단강 서안지구에 거주하는 어린이 60명이 선물 상자를 받았다. 방한복과 기독교 소책자, 영적 자료 등이 전달됐다. 한 가족은 어린이들이 선물을 받고 영적인 격려를 얻었으며, 핍박으로 두려움과 슬픔이 가득한 상황에서도 기쁜 성탄절을 보낼 수 있었다고 전했다.

인도에서는 순교자의 소리 협력기관 두 곳이 사역을 진행해 어린이 375명에게 선물 상자를 전달했다. 만화 성경과 쌀, 책가방, 물병, 학용품, 위생용품, 선물과 초콜릿 등이 포함됐다. 지원받은 어린이들 가운데 상당수는 종교적 차별과 실업, 극심한 빈곤을 겪는 가정 출신이었다.

고아인 디피카(Deepika)는 “적절한 학용품이 없어 학교생활에 어려움을 겪었으며, 교사와 급우들에게 부당한 대우를 받는다고 느껴 학교에 가지 않을 때도 있었다”고 밝혔다. 그러나 선물 상자를 받은 뒤 “알록달록한 이 가방과 학용품 세트와 물병을 받고 나니 학교에 갈 용기가 생겼다”고 말했다.

한국VOM은 올해 전달할 선물 상자의 수량이 모금된 후원금에 따라 결정된다고 밝혔다. 사역에 동참하기 원하는 교회와 성도는 12월 31일까지 한국VOM 웹사이트에서 후원 항목 중 ‘성탄절선물상자’를 선택하거나, 국민은행 463501-01-243303(예금주 사단법인 순교자의 소리)으로 후원금을 보낼 수 있다. 계좌이체 시에는 본인 성명 옆에 ‘성탄절’이라고 기재해야 해당 사역 후원금으로 사용된다.

summary_zh: 300多名德国神学家、牧师和福音派领袖发表公开信，支持因进球庆祝动作表达基督教信仰而陷入争议的足球运动员菲利克斯·恩梅查（Felix Nmecha）。他们敦促多特蒙德足球俱乐部支持该球员，并表示在民主社会中，个人公开宣认和表达自己信仰的权利应得到保障。《福音焦点》（Evangelical Focus）于16日（以下均为当地时间）报道称，300多名德国福音派领袖签署了一封公开信，以支持多特蒙德的中场球员恩梅查。这封题为《声援菲利克斯·恩梅查并呼吁真正宽容》的公开信已转交给俱乐部管理层。26岁的恩梅查在进球后，通过摘下戴在头上的虚拟皇冠并将其放在草坪上的动作来表达自己的基督教信仰。这一庆祝动作将耶稣基督比作“万王之王”。
title_zh: 300多名德国基督教领袖支持足球运动员恩梅查（Lars Rönn Umtiti）的宗教信仰自由
content:
독일의 신학자와 목회자, 복음주의 지도자 300여 명이 기독교 신앙을 표현하는 골 세리머니로 논란에 휩싸인 축구선수 펠릭스 은메차(Felix Nmecha)를 지지하는 공개서한을 발표했다. 이들은 민주주의 사회에서 개인이 자신의 신앙을 공개적으로 고백하고 표현할 권리가 보장돼야 한다며 보루시아 도르트문트 구단에 선수에 대한 지지를 촉구했다.

에반젤리컬 포커스(Evangelical Focus)는 16일(이하 현지시각) 독일 복음주의권 지도자 300여 명이 도르트문트 소속 미드필더 은메차를 지지하는 공개서한에 서명했다고 보도했다. ‘펠릭스 은메차와의 연대 및 진정한 관용을 위한 호소’라는 제목의 해당 서한은 구단 경영진에 전달됐다.

26세의 은메차는 골을 넣은 뒤 머리에 쓴 가상의 왕관을 벗어 잔디 위에 내려놓는 동작으로 자신의 기독교 신앙을 표현해 왔다. 이 세리머니는 예수 그리스도를 ‘왕 중의 왕’으로 고백하며 자신의 왕관을 그분 앞에 내려놓는다는 의미를 담고 있다. ‘왕의 귀환’(The Return of the King)이라는 이름으로 불리며 예수 그리스도의 재림을 상징한다.

논란은 은메차가 복음주의 축구선수 네트워크인 ‘볼러스 인 갓’(Ballers in God)과 연관돼 있다는 사실이 알려지면서 확대됐다. 독일 공영방송 ARD의 보도에 따르면 이 단체는 동성애를 죄로 규정하고 낙태를 ‘사탄의 계획’으로 표현한 바 있다. 도르트문트 구단의 공식 팬 대표 조직은 해당 단체가 특정 집단을 차별하거나 배제하는 관점을 확산시킬 수 있다며 우려를 나타냈다.

은메차는 자신의 세리머니가 특정 단체를 홍보하거나 차별과 혐오를 조장하기 위한 것이 아니라고 해명했다. 그는 SNS를 통해 “내 행동은 왕관을 곧 오실 왕 앞에 내려놓고 예수 그리스도를 가리키기 위한 것”이라며 “기독교의 메시지는 출신과 신념, 세계관에 관계없이 모든 사람을 사랑하고 존중하는 것”이라고 밝혔다.

이에 독일 복음주의권 지도자들은 공개서한을 통해 “은메차 역시 다른 독일 시민과 마찬가지로 자신의 신앙을 실천하고 공개적으로 고백할 권리가 있다”고 강조하며 “서로 다른 세계관이 공존하는 민주주의 법치국가에서 자신의 신앙을 공개적으로 전달하고 옹호하는 일이 가능해야 한다”고 밝혔다.

서명자들은 독일복음주의연맹(EAD) 회장 라인하르트 쉰크(Reinhardt Schink), 설교자 울리히 파르차니(Ulrich Parzany), 아우크스부르크 기도원 설립자 요하네스 하르틀(Johannes Hartl), 독일오픈도어 대표 아르투어 슈뢰터(Artur Schröter), 신학자 롤란트 베르너(Roland Werner) 등을 포함한다. 공개서한을 주도한 요하네스 트라이헬(Johannes Traichel) 목사도 참여했다.

이들은 서한에서 “전통적인 기독교 신앙을 비롯해 생명 보호와 성윤리에 관한 서로 다른 견해를 용인하는 진정한 관용이 약화되고 있다”고 우려했다. 또한 “기독교 신앙을 고백하는 것이 다른 사람을 비하하거나 배제하는 행위와 동일시돼서는 안 된다”고 강조했다. 아울러 “구단이 상호 존중과 관용을 실천하는 데 기여하고 선수의 신앙 표현을 지지해 달라”고 요청했으며, 관련 당사자들과 대화할 의사도 밝혔다.

위르겐 클롭 독일 대표팀 감독은 “은메차와 대화를 나눴으며,그가 모든 사람을 사랑하고 차별하지 않는다는 점을 확인했다”고 밝혔다. 다만 “국가대표팀 경기에서는 앞으로 해당 세리머니를 하지 않기로 선수와 의견을 나눴다”고 전했다. 이와 관련해 은메차가 소속팀 경기에서도 같은 결정을 내릴지는 아직 확인되지 않았다.

한편 독일 개신교 매체 에반겔리쉬데(evangelisch.de)가 소개한 여론조사에서는 응답자의 72%가 “은메차의 세리머니는 부적절하다”고 평가했다. 약 5,000명이 참여한 이번 조사는 기독교 신앙을 가진 응답자들 사이에서도 비슷한 결과를 보였다. 가톨릭 신자의 70%, 개신교 신자의 72%가 해당 세리머니를 부적절하다고 답했다.

title: Maria Rosa Mistica , Pierina Gilli e una devozione che abbraccia il mondo
summary: C’è un tempo per la prudenza istituzionale, un tempo per il silenzio e un tempo in cui la verità della storia e della fede chiede di essere guardata negli occhi, senza più filtri o timori reverenziali
content: C’è un tempo per la prudenza istituzionale, un tempo per il silenzio e un tempo in cui la verità della storia e della fede chiede di essere guardata negli occhi, senza più filtri o timori reverenziali. È questo il clima che si respira oggi attorno al Santuario di Fontanelle a Montichiari dopo che, nel luglio 2024, il Dicastero per la Dottrina della Fede della Santa Sede ha concesso il formale “Nihil obstat“, riconoscendo ufficialmente la bontà dei messaggi e i frutti spirituali legati alla devozione a Maria Rosa Mistica. Un cammino storico che ha trovato un momento di straordinaria sintesi nel II Convegno Internazionale, un appuntamento che ha rimesso al centro non solo la dimensione teologica degli eventi ma soprattutto il profilo umano e spirituale della veggente, Pierina Gilli. I vecchi pregiudizi e il peso di una solitudine A restituire il sapore autentico di quegli anni difficili è stata la testimonianza di Padre Livio Rozzini, sacerdote bresciano originario di Montichiari e oggi presso la Parrocchia Natività di Maria a Roma. Padre Livio ha riavvolto il nastro del tempo tornando alla sua giovinezza e agli inizi del suo percorso sacerdotale, quando accostarsi a Pierina significava fare i conti con un vero e proprio “luogo di disagio” ecclesiale. Nelle sue parole affiora il ricordo di una donna minuta, vestita di scuro, che frequentava la Messa quotidiana alle 9 nel Duomo del paese, guardata per lo più con sospetto e considerata da molti portatrice di disturbi mentali. Emblematico il retroscena raccontato da Padre Livio: l’allora abate, in obbedienza alla Curia, faceva appendere grossi manifesti bilingui (anche in tedesco) sulla porta del Duomo per avvertire i pellegrini che la Chiesa non garantiva sulle apparizioni delle Fontanelle. Manifesti che le guide dei gruppi, arrivate da lontano, regolarmente strappavano e accartocciavano per evitare la delusione dei fedeli. E che dire del primo incontro ravvicinato? Quando il giovane diacono Livio, per fare conversazione dopo che Pierina gli aveva promesso una preghiera per l’ordinazione, le accennò un articolo di Famiglia Cristiana che la catalogava tra i “falsi santuari d’Italia“, la reazione fu immediata: una frase secca e un leggero, affettuoso scappellotto sulla nuca: «Ma tu non crederai a queste cose! Che ne sanno quei giornalisti di quello che vivo e provo?». «Ripensando oggi al nostro primo incontro — confessa Padre Livio — capisco pienamente la sua giustissima reazione. In fondo questa nostra sorella, pur nella sua fragilità, ha portato un peso troppo grande: la solitudine nel vivere una spiritualità profonda e un progetto custodito per i sacerdoti e la Chiesa, senza essere appoggiata o sostenuta da alcuno». Il cuore delle apparizioni: preghiera, penitenza e il mistero delle tre rose Ma qual era l’origine di quella sofferenza e di quel messaggio che Pierina custodiva con tanta tenacia? Le apparizioni della Vergine — iniziate nel 1947 all’ospedale di Montichiari e proseguite successivamente nella zona campestre delle Fontanelle — si caratterizzavano per la straordinaria intensità del richiamo alla preghiera, al sacrificio e alla penitenza, soprattutto per la conversione delle anime consacrate e la santificazione delle vocazioni. Il celebre titolo di Maria Rosa Mistica si manifestava attraverso simboli forti, come le tre rose (bianca, rossa e gialla) portate sul petto dalla Madonna a indicare la preghiera, il sacrificio e la riparazione, in particolare per i sacerdoti e le religiose in difficoltà. Un disegno spirituale profondo che, se all’epoca apparve destabilizzante o difficile da decifrare per i contemporanei, oggi — alla luce dell’apertura dei suoi diari e del vaglio teologico — svela una straordinaria coerenza evangelica incentrata sulla maternità spirituale della Chiesa. title: Papa Leone : La Chiesa ascolti i disoccupati , i giovani che emigrano e gli anziani soli
summary: Una sollecitudine materna, come quella di Maria. Nella cornice della chiesa madre di Buenos Aires, la Cattedrale della Santissima Trinità, Papa Leone si rivolge all’episcopato argentina e alle équipe
content: Una sollecitudine materna, come quella di Maria. Nella cornice della chiesa madre di Buenos Aires, la Cattedrale della Santissima Trinità, Papa Leone si rivolge all’episcopato argentina e alle équipe sinodali esortandoli a seguire l’esempio della Vergine, presenza che si ravvisa in ogni angolo di questo Paese del Sud America, nella loro missione pastorale. Un compito da svolgere nell’unità delle differenze, data la varietà delle Chiese particolari sul suolo argentino. Il Santo Padre ha inoltre ricordato il suo predecessore Francesco, cui ha reso omaggio con una corona di fiori, e i Beati Mamerto Esquiú, Enrique Angelelli ed Eduardo Pironio. “I santi continuano a formare santi”, ha detto Leone. La presenza mariana “Eminenze, Eccellenze, cari membri delle equipe sinodali, fratelli e sorelle tutti in Cristo Gesù! Vorrei che in questo momento di preghiera percorressimo insieme, con il pensiero, le diverse regioni di questo splendido Paese. In ciascuna delle sue province, la nostra fede ha messo radici in popoli e culture diverse, dando vita a espressioni proprie della vita cristiana, senza perdere l’unità che nasce da Cristo. Pensiamo al nord-ovest, alla sua fede semplice e alle sue profonde devozioni. Andiamo sulla costa, con i suoi grandi fiumi e i suoi campi seminati di futuro. Attraversiamo il nord-est, per lasciarci stupire dalle sue meravigliose cascate e dalle sue vaste piantagioni di yerba mate, che contraddistinguono le usanze di tutto il Cono Sur. Avviciniamoci alla regione del Cuyo, dove i vigneti rallegrano il cuore dell’uomo. Attraversiamo la Pampa e apprezziamo la saggezza di chi lavora la terra. Saliamo sulle sierras e, dall’alto, ammiriamo i doni del creato. Andiamo a sud, dove il freddo e i deserti non impediscono la calda accoglienza della fede. In questa varietà geografica e culturale troviamo una presenza materna che accompagna i suoi abitanti e verso la quale il popolo esprime il proprio affetto con processioni e pellegrinaggi, lungo percorsi di fede e di promesse compiuti a piedi o a cavallo, con poesie, preghiere e canti che si levano in onore del suo nome. Parlo dell’Immacolata Vergine Maria, che questo popolo venera con diversi titoli: la Santissima Vergine del Miracolo, Nostra Signora della Valle, la Vergine del Rosario, Maria di Itatí, Nostra Signora di Luján. Ella, che rimase unita agli Apostoli nella preghiera, accompagna anche oggi la Chiesa che annuncia il suo Figlio (cfr At 1,14). In ogni angolo di questa terra mariana, dalle grandi città ai paesini più piccoli, ci sono fratelli che attendono di conoscere la Buona Novella del Vangelo. Per questo assume un significato particolare il motto di questo Viaggio Apostolico: Benvenuti tutti. Andate e annunciate!”. La festa della Dedicazione “Dopo aver percorso il Paese con l’immaginazione e aver rinnovato il nostro desiderio di andare a evangelizzare, rivolgiamo ora lo sguardo a questa Cattedrale, dove siamo qui riuniti. È provvidenziale poter celebrare i secondi Vespri della Dedicazione di San Giovanni in Laterano, «madre e capo di tutte le chiese dell’Urbe e dell’Orbe», in questa splendida Cattedrale della Santissima Trinità, chiesa madre di Buenos Aires, dove riposano, inoltre, le spoglie del generale José Francisco de San Martín, Padre della Patria. La festa della dedicazione della Basilica Lateranense ci invita a contemplare il mistero della Chiesa, edificata su Cristo, pietra angolare, nella quale tutti noi, come pietre vive, siamo chiamati a formare una dimora spirituale (cfr 1Pt 2,4-5). Il fatto che San Giovanni in Laterano sia la Cattedrale del Vescovo di Roma conferisce a questa celebrazione un particolare significato di comunione con la Sede di Pietro, e tale legame diventa particolarmente intenso celebrandola in questa Cattedrale, la cui cattedra è stata occupata dal nostro caro Papa Francesco prima che fosse chiamato a pascere la Chiesa universale. title: San León Magno : el Papa que defendió la fe y la civilización cristiana – INFOVATICANA
summary: El “Tomus ad Flavianum”: piedra angular del dogma cristológico León Magno fue un teólogo de precisión y profundidad extraordinarias. Su famosa carta doctrinal al patriarca Flaviano de Constantinopla —
content: El “Tomus ad Flavianum”: piedra angular del dogma cristológico León Magno fue un teólogo de precisión y profundidad extraordinarias. Su famosa carta doctrinal al patriarca Flaviano de Constantinopla —conocida como el Tomus ad Flavianum— definió con claridad la doctrina católica sobre las dos naturalezas de Cristo: divina y humana, unidas en una sola Persona. Este documento fue leído en el Concilio de Calcedonia (451) ante cientos de obispos que, al escucharlo, exclamaron: “Pedro ha hablado por boca de León.” Con esa expresión, la Iglesia universal reconocía el primado de la sede romana y la continuidad entre el Apóstol Pedro y sus sucesores. En tiempos en que el poder imperial pretendía someter la doctrina al control político, León reivindicó que la autoridad del Papa no depende del César ni de los concilios, sino de Cristo mismo, que prometió: “Tú eres Pedro, y sobre esta piedra edificaré mi Iglesia.” Gracias a su intervención, el Concilio de Calcedonia se convirtió en un hito de la ortodoxia cristológica y en un testimonio de la primacía del Romano Pontífice. El Papa León no impuso su autoridad con la fuerza, sino con la verdad; no por ambición humana, sino por fidelidad al depósito recibido. El Papa que detuvo a Atila En el año 452, la amenaza de los hunos llegó hasta las puertas de Italia. Atila, llamado “el azote de Dios”, había devastado Europa central y avanzaba hacia Roma. Sin ejército ni armas, León decidió ir al encuentro del invasor acompañado solo de algunos clérigos. El encuentro en el río Mincio, cerca de Mantua, se convirtió en uno de los episodios más sobrecogedores de la historia. La tradición narra que Atila, al ver al Papa, quedó sobrecogido por una fuerza sobrenatural y decidió retirarse. Algunos cronistas antiguos dicen que el caudillo vio detrás de León a los santos Pedro y Pablo empuñando espadas. Fuera cual fuera la causa, el hecho histórico es indiscutible: el Papa, solo con su autoridad moral, salvó a Roma de una destrucción segura. Tres años después, en el 455, León volvió a intervenir ante el vándalo Genserico, quien, aunque saqueó la ciudad, accedió a no incendiarla ni matar a sus habitantes. En una era de barbarie y desesperanza, el Papa se convirtió en defensor de la dignidad humana y de la civilización cristiana naciente. Un pastor de almas y doctor de la fe Más allá de los hechos históricos, el legado espiritual de León Magno se encuentra en sus Sermones y Cartas, textos que combinan rigor teológico, belleza retórica y profundidad pastoral. Sus homilías sobre la Encarnación y la Pascua son verdaderas joyas del pensamiento cristiano. En ellas resuena una teología que no separa la doctrina de la vida, ni la fe de la caridad. Fue también un reformador eclesial: disciplinó al clero, combatió los abusos, promovió la vida monástica y fortaleció la autoridad episcopal. Instituyó la solemnidad de la Natividad del Señor en Roma y consolidó la liturgia romana, que más tarde se extendería a toda la cristiandad. En un tiempo en que el caos amenazaba con disolver las instituciones, León mostró que la verdadera reforma de la Iglesia comienza en la santidad de sus pastores. De su espiritualidad brota una enseñanza perenne: el cristiano no puede dejarse arrastrar por el miedo ni por la confusión del mundo. Como escribió en una de sus homilías más célebres: “Reconoce, cristiano, tu dignidad. Y, puesto que has sido hecho partícipe de la naturaleza divina, no vuelvas a la antigua vileza con una conducta indigna.” En esas palabras se resume toda su visión: la fe no es una idea, sino una transformación de la persona; una participación real en la vida de Cristo. El Doctor que iluminó siglos León Magno murió el 10 de noviembre del año 461. Fue sepultado en la Basílica de San Pedro y proclamado Doctor de la Iglesia en el siglo XVIII por el Papa Benedicto XIV. title: Quando o escutismo católico deixa de ser católico
summary: 1.A Associação de Guias e Escuteiros Católicos Italianos (AGECI) eliminou, muito recentemente, a orientação sexual e a identidade de género como critérios de recrutamento e selecção daqueles que prete
content: 1.A Associação de Guias e Escuteiros Católicos Italianos (AGECI) eliminou, muito recentemente, a orientação sexual e a identidade de género como critérios de recrutamento e selecção daqueles que pretendem, no âmbito da missão do adulto no escutismo, exercer responsabilidades educativas. É uma decisão relevante, que suscita reflexão e debate. O que está em causa não é uma mera alteração administrativa ou organizativa, nem uma actualização do sistema de progresso ou do uniforme. O que está em causa é algo estruturante, que tem a ver com a própria natureza e essência do Movimento Escutista, em particular do Escutismo Católico. A questão não é saber se pessoas com atracção pelo mesmo sexo podem ou não fazer parte de um agrupamento; não se pretende indagar da vida íntima dos membros, nem perseguir ou excluir alguém por causa da sua orientação. A igual dignidade de todos os seres humanos, criados à imagem de Deus, constitui um valor inegociável. A questão que se coloca é outra: que modelo de ser humano o Escutismo Católico propõe às crianças e aos adolescentes através dos seus educadores; e isto sim, é algo que nos deve interpelar profundamente. 2. Todo o processo educativo, também no escutismo, não é neutro ou vazio de sentidos; tem sempre por base uma determinada visão do Homem, da Sociedade e do mundo, ou seja, uma determinada cosmovisão, neste caso, cristã. É por isso que adquire enorme importância garantir que os grandes documentos orientadores do escutismo católico sejam, em toda a sua pedagogia, permeados pela visão cristã do Homem e da sociedade. E é igualmente importante garantir, naquilo que humanamente é possível garantir, que os Chefes, enquanto educadores chamados a levar a cabo essa missão, tenham o perfil adequado para tão elevada tarefa. É por isso que vemos com perplexidade e apreensão que uma importante organização que se apresenta como católica renuncie explicitamente a avaliar a adequação antropológica e moral daqueles que se tornarão referências para crianças e adolescentes, precisamente numa idade em que procuram exemplos e modelos para além da esfera estritamente familiar. 3. Não se trata de questionar a dignidade pessoal de quem quer que seja, que é inegável e deve sempre ser respeitada. Como recorda o Catecismo da Igreja Católica, as pessoas com tendências homossexuais devem ser acolhidas com respeito, compaixão e delicadeza, ee para com elas toda a forma de discriminação injusta (cf. CEC 2358-2359). Importa por isso distinguir com clareza três planos: a pessoa, sempre digna de acolhimento; a tendência ou atracção, que não é em si mesma culpa moral; e os comportamentos e opções de vida livremente assumidos e publicamente testemunhadovitando-ss. A questão que se coloca a um movimento da Igreja não é a da dignidade da pessoa, mas a da coerência do testemunho educativo: são aceitáveis, em quem educa em nome da Igreja, comportamentos, opções e estilos de vida assumidos de forma estável e declarada em conflito com a visão cristã da sexualidade? A orientação sexual ou a identidade de género não podem ser consideradas irrelevantes para o discernimento educativo sem se assumir implicitamente que a antropologia católica sobre o homem, a mulher, a sua igual dignidade, complementaridade e reciprocidade, seria irrelevante. Esta exigência de clareza moral e de coerência de vida não se dirige apenas a pessoas homossexuais; dirige-se a todos os educadores, heterossexuais incluídos, chamados à castidade segundo o próprio estado de vida, à fidelidade matrimonial, ao respeito pela vida nascente e a uma afectividade ordenada. Só assim podem constituir-se como modelos credíveis para os jovens, ajudando-os a construir de forma integrada a sua personalidade e identidade. É isto que credibiliza e dá coerência ao método escutista enquanto movimento educativo, e que lhe confere uma sabedoria, uma mística e uma identidade propriamente católicas. 4. Vivemos um tempo em que proliferam ideias que se assemelham à fé, que usam o seu vocab

title: El papa León XIV ya está en Argentina y el campo tuvo protagonismo en su primer discurso
summary: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país
content: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país desde Juan Pablo II en 1987. En ese marco, la primera actividad del Sumo Pontífice fue un discurso en el Palacio Libertad de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires (CABA), frente al presidente de la Nación, Javier Milei. Y aunque sus palabras lógicamente estuvieron apuntadas hacia toda la sociedad, hubo numerosos pasajes que encontraron especial sintonía con el mundo agropecuario. Esto, en la previa de la reunión que León XIV mantendrá el lunes con representantes empresariales, sindicales y de organizaciones sociales, entre los que estarán los presidentes de las cuatro entidades de la Mesa de Enlace. EL PAPA LEÓN XIV EN ARGENTINA Puntualmente, el jefe mayor del Vaticano destacó el valor del esfuerzo cotidiano de los argentinos, con una mención expresa a quienes trabajan en el campo, y reivindicó la importancia de generar oportunidades, estimular la iniciativa privada y aprovechar responsablemente los recursos naturales. “Esta tierra conoce bien el valor del esfuerzo de quienes se ganan la vida en el campo y en las ciudades”, expresó León XIV, al destacar también el papel de los emprendedores y de las familias que sostienen sus hogares a través del trabajo. Asimismo, el Papa reconoció el enorme potencial productivo del país, al señalar que la Argentina cuenta con una extraordinaria riqueza natural, desde sus campos y reservas de agua hasta sus fuentes de energía, minerales y biodiversidad. Así, su mensaje combinó la posibilidad de aprovechar esos recursos para generar desarrollo y bienestar con la responsabilidad de preservar el ambiente y las condiciones de vida de las futuras generaciones. También dedicó un espacio a la innovación, la investigación y las nuevas tecnologías, incluida la inteligencia artificial, destacando su capacidad para transformar la producción y mejorar la vida de las personas. Por otro lado, al expresar una mirada sobre América del Sur, mencionó además a los alimentos, la energía y el conocimiento como elementos que vinculan a los países y abren oportunidades para fortalecer la cooperación regional. LEON XIV, EL MARTÍN FIERO Y EL MATE Asimismo, León XIV ofreció referencias cargadas de simbolismo para la identidad argentina. Por ejemplo, mencionó al Martín Fierro de José Hernández, a Jorge Luis Borges, al tango y a las tradiciones del interior del país. Y no faltó una de las costumbres más arraigadas entre los argentinos: el mate compartido, al que presentó como un gesto cotidiano que favorece la conversación y la cercanía. Por último, hacia el final de su intervención, León XIV evocó a Nuestra Señora de Luján, patrona de la Argentina y figura de especial significado para las comunidades rurales y para generaciones de familias de todo el país. También recordó al papa Francisco, citó a Carlos Gardel y alentó a los argentinos a valorar el patrimonio recibido de las generaciones anteriores y trabajar para dejar un país mejor a quienes vendrán. De esta manera, sin ser un discurso específicamente dirigido al agro, las palabras de León XIV dejaron un reconocimiento al trabajo rural, a la producción, a la iniciativa emprendedora y a las tradiciones que forman parte de la identidad argentina. Un mensaje que también llegó al corazón del campo argentino. EL DISCURSO COMPLETO DEL PAPA LEÓN XIV Señor Presidente de la República, distinguidas autoridades y miembros del cuerpo diplomático. Señoras y señores, me alegra profundamente encontrarme hoy en esta querida tierra argentina. Agradezco, señor Presidente, las cordiales palabras que ha tenido a bien dirigirme y la acogida que por medio de usted me brinda su pueblo. Saludos también a los miembros del cuerpo diplomático y a las demás autoridades aquí presentes, y extiendo con afecto mi saludo a todos los argentinos. title: Papa Leone : Lautorità intesa come servizio è orientata al bene comune
summary: Primo discorso della seconda tappa del viaggio apostolico di Papa Leone XIV in Sud America. Parlando al Palacio Libertad a Buenos Aires, di fronte alle autorità, alla società civile e al corpo diploma
content: Primo discorso della seconda tappa del viaggio apostolico di Papa Leone XIV in Sud America. Parlando al Palacio Libertad a Buenos Aires, di fronte alle autorità, alla società civile e al corpo diplomatico argentini, il Santo Padre ha ricordato che ogni generazione riceve ine eredità dalla precedente il proprio Paese e a sua volta partecipa alla sua costruzione, imparando a discernere cosa va conservato. Il patrimonio comune, ha aggiunto Leone, comprende anche la democrazia, che chiede all’autorità di intendere il proprio compito come servizio orientato al bene comune a partire dalle condizioni concrete della vita delle persone, come le famiglie e i giovani, che devono poter ricevere opportunità professionali ed educazione per realizzare i propri progetti di vita senza il peso dell’incertezza o dover andare altrove. Il saluto “Signor Presidente della Repubblica, distinte Autorità e membri del Corpo diplomatico, Signore e Signori,sono molto lieto di trovarmi oggi in questa cara Terra argentina. La ringrazio, Signor Presidente, per le cordiali parole che ha voluto rivolgermi e per l’accoglienza che, attraverso di Lei, mi riserva il suo Popolo. Saluto inoltre i membri del Corpo diplomatico e le altre Autorità presenti, ed estendo con affetto il mio saluto a tutti gli Argentini. “Sono venuto come Successore dell’Apostolo Pietro e, pertanto, come Pastore. Desidero incontrare la Chiesa in cammino in questa Terra e rivolgermi anche all’intera Nazione e a coloro ai quali è stato affidato il compito di servirla. La Chiesa accompagna la vita dei popoli attraverso la missione che le è stata affidata. Per questo, anche nei confronti di coloro che ricoprono cariche pubbliche, desidera offrire una parola ispirata al Vangelo e volta a tutelare la dignità di ogni persona, la concordia e il bene comune“. Un’ampia storia “Venire in questa terra ha, per me, un significato particolare. Per dodici anni la Chiesa universale ha ascoltato la voce di un Pontefice argentino, che ha portato con sé, nella memoria e nel cuore, i luoghi, le persone e la fede che qui ha ricevuto. Oggi, succedendogli nel Ministero petrino, percorro in un certo senso la strada inversa e vengo nella Patria dove Papa Francesco ha iniziato un cammino, che in seguito si sarebbe intrecciato con quello di tutta la Chiesa. Avvicinarmi alla terra in cui è cresciuto significa anche avvicinarmi a una storia molto più ampia, fatta di generazioni di uomini e donne che, prima e dopo di lui, hanno accolto questa Patria e vi hanno lasciato qualcosa di sé. Alcuni sono nati qui; altri sono giunti da lontano e vi hanno trovato una casa; altri ancora appartengono a popoli indigeni, la cui presenza precede la nascita della Nazione. Da quell’incontro fra origini ed esperienze diverse ha preso forma, col passare del tempo, un Popolo che ha saputo aprire le proprie porte, fare spazio a chi arrivava e mantenere, anche nei momenti difficili, una notevole capacità di rialzarsi e andare avanti. Tutti hanno contribuito a plasmare l’Argentina che oggi ho la gioia di visitare”. Il patrimonio comune “Nessuna generazione costruisce la Patria partendo da zero. La riceve. Lo fa attraverso una lingua e legami che l’hanno preceduta; attraverso istituzioni fondate da altri e beni che sono cresciuti grazie al lavoro di molti. La storia custodisce motivi di gratitudine, ma anche ricordi dolorosi. Spetta a ogni generazione discernere ciò che merita di essere conservato, affrontare le conseguenze ingiuste del passato e accrescere il patrimonio materiale e spirituale comune. La patria che oggi è nelle vostre mani sarà domani l’eredità di altri”. title: Why Did Prosecutors Agree To Omit References to Katy Perry From the Opening Statements at Trial ?
summary: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November
content: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November 2026, after a jury returned verdicts at Southwark Crown Court. Brand, 51, was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women. Jurors acquitted him of two further rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault. He had denied all seven charges, which concerned six women. Details of the pretrial discussions became public after reporting restrictions ended. They showed how Brand's former marriage was kept out of the prosecution's opening address, although he later mentioned Perry while giving evidence. Why Katy Perry References Were Removed From the Opening Lead prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC acknowledged in written submissions that references to Brand's relationship with Perry after 2009 'may be sensitive'. According to Sky News' court reporting, prosecutors were 'content to remove these from the opening' following defence submissions. The agreement was limited to the opening statement. It did not prevent every mention of Perry during the proceedings or establish that the relationship itself was evidence of wrongdoing. Perry was not accused of any offence. Prosecutors also agreed to leave out references to Brand's earlier religious beliefs and his 2024 baptism. His Christian conversion was nevertheless mentioned during questioning of his wife, Laura, showing that the restrictions on the opening did not cover all subsequent testimony. Other arguments before the trial concerned references to Brand's past drug and alcohol use. His lawyers challenged their relevance to the allegations, and material about treatment at a sex addiction clinic was omitted from a former assistant's evidence. Those disputes were separate from the agreement concerning Perry. The Crown Prosecution Service confirmed that investigators had not asked Perry for a witness statement. Senior Crown Prosecutor David Roberts said reasonable lines of inquiry relevant to the charges had been pursued. There is no basis in that statement to suggest Perry refused to cooperate. Katy Perry's Marriage Still Entered the Courtroom Perry and Brand began dating in 2009 and married in Rajasthan, India, in 2010. They separated in December 2011, and their divorce was finalised in 2012. The offences for which Brand was convicted took place between 2004 and 2009. During his evidence, Brand referred to the marriage and said it had brought him 'staggering fame'. The comment arose from his own testimony, not the prosecution's opening statement. It did not turn Perry into a witness or complainant. The Crown Prosecution Service said the women whose cases resulted in convictions came forward independently after a television investigation aired in September 2023. Prosecutors relied on their accounts and testimony from other witnesses to present evidence of Brand's conduct. Following the verdict, Roberts said Brand had 'used his celebrity status to commit sexual crimes'. The agency thanked the women for coming forward and stressed that sexual offences can be prosecuted years after they occur. The complainants have lifelong anonymity. Mr Justice Joel Bennathan refused Brand bail and remanded him in custody ahead of sentencing on Monday, 9 November. The judge warned that he faced a 'significant custodial term'. Rape carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment in England and Wales. © Copyright IBTimes 2026. All rights reserved.

title: Discovering Jewish roots, responding to antisemitism
summary: By Charles Gardner — My wife Linda had no idea of the Jewish background of her employers during the 1970s and 80s. So we travelled down to London for an exhibition of the Salmon and […]  The post  Discovering Jewish roots, responding to antisemitism  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Charles Gardner — Charles and Linda on their wedding day My wife Linda had no idea of the Jewish background of her employers during the 1970s and 80s. She just knew that she loved working for them and only left to follow God’s call to work with children. So we travelled down to London for an exhibition of the Salmon and Gluckstein dynasty, and the story of how these resilient Jewish families fled violent persecution in Eastern Europe to build what became the largest catering company in the world known as J Lyons & Co. Linda worked there as a home economist from 1977-1984 but it was only much later that she learnt of the Jewish nature of the firm that once literally fed Britain with its teashops and corner houses on every high street, and its products in every home, Linda playing her part through her cooking and marketing skills. A few years later, after graduating from Bible College in Bournemouth, she worked at a prayer and reconciliation centre in Northern Ireland where she was introduced to the importance of the Christian faith’s Jewish roots, as a result of which she took a study tour of Israel to learn more. And on a second trip to the Holy Land ten years later, she got more than she bargained for. At Cana in Galilee, where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding, Linda was given a vision of her own wedding. And we met on a blind date six months later! Though having Jewish ancestry myself, I grew up knowing nothing about it. But I learnt more later, especially after becoming a Christian in my early twenties, as Linda had done. It helped that I had a Jewish believer as my early mentor, and I became increasingly aware of the significance of our Jewish heritage, about which I now write prolifically. Meanwhile Linda, who has been teaching Christianity in Doncaster area schools for over 30 years, also now teaches about Judaism as it forms the context into which Christ came to us, fulfilling all the laws and promises of the Old Testament. So in both our cases, we were kept in the dark about very important aspects of our lives – until the Lord shone his light on the truth. Which brings me to the Christian Church as a whole, especially in the UK. We have known very little, if anything, of our faith’s Jewish roots or of God’s ongoing purposes for Israel. This needs to change – and fast! For we are surely hurtling towards the Messiah’s Second Coming like a high-speed train, in danger of coming off the rails with the rest of humanity if we fail to get to grips with how we Christians fit into the unfolding picture of global opposition to tiny Israel. What is our role as we watch antisemitism spread across the globe like wildfire? Do we just sit and watch, or write it off as having nothing to do with us, and remain silent? Or do we stand up to be counted as those who refuse to salute the new Nazism that portrays itself as anti-Zionism – a Confessing Church walking the way of the cross for God’s chosen people? My questions come as renewed calls are made for an independent inquiry into antisemitism at the BBC following news that Oscar-winning producer Lucie Kon has won £400,000 in compensation from the broadcaster. Lucie’s career is said to have unravelled after she raised concerns about antisemitism within the BBC, though the latter have not admitted to any fault. title: New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran
summary: By Howard Cooper — Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, says he plans to take his oath of office on a Quran when the new Congress convenes in January. El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers on November 3, becoming the first Muslim American elected to the […]  The post  New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Howard Cooper — Abdul Al-Sayed (wikipedia commons) Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, says he plans to take his oath of office on a Quran when the new Congress convenes in January. El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers on November 3, becoming the first Muslim American elected to the Senate and the first epidemiologist to serve in the chamber, according to WION News. In an interview with NPR’s Leila Fadel, he said, “I will likely swear on a Quran. Which Quran, we’re not sure.” He pointed to a copy once owned by Thomas Jefferson, which Keith Ellison used when he was sworn in to Congress, and to an old Quran at the University of Michigan that he described as the first in the state. The US Constitution does not require a Bible or any religious text. In practice, senators usually take the formal oath together on the Senate floor, and a Bible comes into play in individual ceremonial swearings-in. El-Sayed hasn’t said whether he’ll use the Quran in the formal proceedings, the ceremony, or both, and that his choice would not alter the wording of the oath. He has also stressed that his oath will be to the U.S. Constitution,  according to IBTimes. He will be sworn in by Vice President JD Vance, a fact El-Sayed has noted with humor. The Blaze reported he called it a “delicious irony” that Vance is constitutionally required to do so. Not everyone is comfortable with the news. The Daily Signal reported that former White House press secretary Sean Spicer said this week that given El-Sayed’s connections and statements, he should undergo a formal background check before receiving classified information. Presumably, Spicer was referring to Al-Sayed’s family connections to the Muslim Brotherhood. For many Christians, the moment raises questions about the role of faith in public life, the long American tradition of religious liberty, and the Judeo-Christian roots of the United States. El-Sayed and his colleagues are scheduled to be sworn in at noon on January 3, 2027. The post New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran first appeared on God Reports .

title: Yemeni journalist visits Israel, dramatically changes views
summary: By Charles Gardner — A brave Yemeni journalist has stunned the United Nations with an account of how his view of Israel has dramatically changed following a visit there. And he was led to the conclusion that everything he has been taught to believe about the Jews is a lie. Luai Ahmed was invited to […]  The post  Yemeni journalist visits Israel, dramatically changes views  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Charles Gardner — Luai Ahmed speaking at UN (screenshot YouTube) A brave Yemeni journalist has stunned the United Nations with an account of how his view of Israel has dramatically changed following a visit there. And he was led to the conclusion that everything he has been taught to believe about the Jews is a lie. Luai Ahmed was invited to address the assembly by UN Watch, a non-governmental organisation monitoring the international body’s performance, as the UN Human Rights Council gathered to debate racism. He said: “I grew up in Yemen, where the word that we used for black people is ‘abeed’, which quite literally means ‘slaves’. Racism towards black people in my country is horrifying, but it’s not even the most toxic hatred that I was taught. “The first time I ever heard the word ‘Jew’ was in my local mosque when I was nine years old. At the end of Friday prayers, the Imam said: ‘May Allah kill the Jews and the Zionists’. And I responded alongside thousands of Muslims praying beside me: ‘Ameen’.” Luai then continued: “I was taught that Zionism meant killing Arabs, stealing our land, and destroying Islam. Then October 7th came. Hamas terrorists ‘freed Palestine’ by slaughtering 1,200 Israelis and kidnapping more than 200 people, including a one-year-old child. “Almost everyone in my Arab-Muslim circle celebrated. I didn’t. Instead, as a journalist, I decided to visit the so-called Zionist entity, and I was completely shocked to the core by the lack of apartheid and racism that I experienced. “One day, I got an eye infection. At the hospital, the nurses in reception were Jewish. The doctor treating me was Arab. Is there racism in Israel? Of course. There’s racism everywhere. “But Arabs in Israel aren’t called ‘slaves’. They are doctors, engineers, and party leaders. My experience helped me realise that Zionism really just means the Jewish people’s right to a tiny country. Everything I was taught was a lie.” Quite apart from tipping over the tables of woke left-wing ideology spreading its poisonous antisemitic tentacles across the globe, Luai’s testimony also knocks holes into the escalating pressure on the UK to make reparations for the slave trade, which saw plenty of collaborators in the host countries of those who suffered. And of course, the truth that dare not speak its name – that it was Christians like William Wilberforce who put an end to it! Luai is a great inspiration to fellow journalists like me who long for more of our colleagues to stand up and be counted. Thanks also to David Soakell of Christian Friends of Israel’s Watching Over Zion newsletter, November 5, 2026. title: Manta ray led marine scientist to lost fin
summary: By Mark Ellis — Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, […]  The post  Manta ray led marine scientist to lost fin  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Mark Ellis — Amber Sparks (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, especially with the Rigs-to-Reefs program, when oil drilling platforms are decommissioned. “We work with the oil companies to repurpose certain parts of the platform, retrofit it so that it can remain in place and continue to function as an artificial reef,” she told God Reports. Amber’s work has taken her around the world, with many dive experiences and encounters in the ocean with marine life. But there is one story she will never forget. It happened in the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Amber graduated from Scripps Institute and was invited on a research industry cruise with oil company representatives, scientists, and regulators on a liveaboard vessel. At the Flower Garden National Banks, a marine protected area 200 miles offshore, Amber was excited about her first dive, but slightly nervous. “You don’t know what you’re going to see or what this experience is going to be like,” she recalls. Dropping in (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook) Each diver had to jump off the vessel to get in the water. “We’re all geared up with our snorkel, our buoyancy control device, our wetsuit, and fins are the last thing you put on. So, I put on my fins and I jumped off the side of the boat.” “The second that I hit the water, one of my fins fell off, and I looked down and watched as it slowly descended to the bottom.” Amber glanced over at her dive buddy, and said, “I’m gonna go down. I’m going down.” Normally she would wait for her dive partner and they would go down together, but in this case, she thought, “I can’t (wait). I gotta go get my fin.” So Amber slowly began to descend to the bottom, about 60 feet below the ocean surface. “I felt completely lost. I was in a completely new area. I never dove before, and now I only had one fin.” She realized there were major currents that could have moved her fin in any direction. “I realized I can’t really swim with just one fin. So now not only am I at depth, but I’m handicapped with just one fin, and I started to feel pretty nervous.” It would probably take her 10 minutes to get back the surface, with safety stops. At the moment before panic set in, she looked upward and saw an amazing sight. It was a giant manta ray, with wings extending at least 10 feet. “Its wingspan was double mine. Its arms were out, and it was coming up over the side of a reef. “I’ve never seen a manta ray like this before. It totally took my breath away, it was so magnificent.” Another manta ray (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) She noted that manta rays are known in the ocean community to be “majestic, God-connected creatures with an understanding maybe beyond what humans can fully comprehend. They see the world and feel it in another way,” she notes. Mantas have the largest known brain of any fish. Their brains are large in absolute terms and relative to body size, which is also true of elephants, dolphins, and people. Their brains have enlarged areas associated with intelligence, vision, and motor coordination, and some of their brain cells are more like those in birds and mammals than in other fish.(1) As the manta ray drew close to Amber, she had an unusual communication experience. “I felt this sense where it said, ‘I want you to follow me. I’m going to help you find your fin.’ Amber Sparks Amber’s diving partner had just descended next to her, and they both began to swim after the manta. “I was barely making it, following this manta ray across the reef. At this point, I was so excited to see a manta ray. I kind of forgot about being handicapped, and I was just trying to go as fast as I can to keep up with it. Then Amber got the sur

title: Houston’s Epiphanies: Turrell and Rothko
summary: The word epiphany is defined by the Oxford Learner’s Dictionary as “a sudden and surprising moment of understanding.” Often, such epiphany moments arrive unexpectedly, interrupting the ordinary rhythms of life with extraordinary insight. Sometimes they come through a conversation, a passage of Scripture, or an encounter with nature. Other times, they emerge through art. content: The word epiphany is defined by the Oxford Learner’s Dictionary as “a sudden and surprising moment of understanding.” Often, such epiphany moments arrive unexpectedly, interrupting the ordinary rhythms of life with extraordinary insight. Sometimes they come through a conversation, a passage of Scripture, or an encounter with nature. Other times, they emerge through art. Twilight Epiphany. Photo: Eliott Davis Sitting beneath artist James Turrell’s Twilight Epiphany on the campus of Rice University in Houston, Texas, on a Sunday morning as the sun rose, the word epiphany took on new meaning. As the morning light slowly illuminated the sky, subtle shifts in color transformed the space above me. The experience was both architectural and atmospheric, a convergence of art, nature, and contemplation. Turrell, born in 1943, is an American artist internationally recognized for his exploration of light, space, and human perception. Raised in the Quaker tradition, Turrell’s artistic vision reflects an appreciation for silence, stillness, and inward reflection. Commissioned by Rice University through the generosity of alumna Suzanne Deal Booth, Twilight Epiphany opened in 2012 as part of the university’s public art program. The pyramidal Skyspace, designed to accommodate approximately 120 visitors, features an aperture in its roof through which viewers observe the changing sky. At sunrise and sunset, carefully programmed LED lights interact with the natural atmosphere, creating an extraordinary experience of shifting color and perception. More than a work of architecture, the installation invites visitors to slow down, look upward, and reconsider the relationship between light and the world around them. James Turrell (Chat GPT) For me, the experience was something of a spiritual exercise. Light, after all, is among the Bible’s most enduring metaphors for divine revelation, truth, and beauty. As the colors shifted above me, I was reminded that beauty does not always announce itself loudly. Sometimes it simply asks us to be still and pay attention. Rothko Chapel. Photo: https://www.mark-rothko.org/rothko-chapel.jsp#google_vignette. From Rice University, I headed to another meditative landmark: the Rothko Chapel . Here, I sat among the monumental, dark-hued paintings of Mark Rothko, contemplating both the tragedy of the artist’s life and the triumph of the chapel that bears his name. Commissioned by Houston philanthropists John and Dominique de Menil in 1964 and dedicated in 1971, the Rothko Chapel is an interfaith sanctuary devoted to contemplation, spiritual reflection, and human rights. Its octagonal interior contains fourteen large-scale paintings by Rothko, whose subtle variations of black, maroon, and purple create an atmosphere of profound stillness. Rothko, born Marcus Rothkowitz in 1903, was a leading figure in American Abstract Expressionism, celebrated for his ability to evoke deep emotional responses through color and form. Yet his personal life was marked by physical illness, depression, and emotional turmoil. In February 1970, before the chapel’s dedication, Rothko died by suicide at the age of sixty-six. He never witnessed the completed sanctuary that would become one of his most enduring artistic legacies. Twilight Epiphany. Photo: Brian C. Nixon There is something deeply moving about this juxtaposition. An artist whose life ended in despair left behind a place where countless visitors have sought peace, meaning, and solace. The darkness of Rothko’s paintings does not necessarily communicate hopelessness. Rather, their quiet intensity invites viewers to confront the depths of human experience—sorrow, longing, mystery, and perhaps even transcendence. Where Turrell’s Twilight Epiphany draws the eyes upward toward the heavens, Rothko’s chapel seems to draw the gaze inward, toward the mysteries of the human soul. One is animated by the changing light of the sky, the other by the stillness of darkened canvases. Yet both offer some

title: Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success
summary: While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence […]  The post  Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: John Warwick Montgomery While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. content: What do Jesus and Isaiah have in common? Quite a bit, according to renowned British New Testament scholar N. T. Wright. Gathering at the marvelous Lanier Theological Library in Houston, Texas—the brainchild of noted attorney, author, and biblical scholar Mark Lanier—Wright offered a packed house in the Great Room a fascinating glimpse into the relationship between the Old Testament prophet Isaiah and the life, ministry, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Dr. Joseph Holden of Veritas International University listening to Dr. NT Wright at Lanier Library. For Wright, Isaiah is far more than an ancient prophetic voice whose words occasionally appear in the New Testament. Rather, the prophet provides a theological framework for understanding Jesus and the unfolding purposes of God. In his book Into the Heart of Isaiah , Wright invites readers to rediscover the extraordinary depth of Isaiah’s prophetic vision, demonstrating how its themes of judgment, restoration, redemption, and new creation find their ultimate expression in Christ. Central to Wright’s interpretation is the conviction that Isaiah’s message cannot be separated from the larger story of Israel. The prophet speaks of exile and homecoming, divine judgment and covenant faithfulness, suffering and salvation. These themes, Wright argues, become essential to understanding how Jesus understood his own mission and how the earliest Christians interpreted his life. Particularly significant is Isaiah’s portrayal of the suffering servant, whose affliction becomes the means through which God’s redemptive purposes are accomplished. Wright connects this prophetic imagery to Jesus’ sacrificial death, while emphasizing that the cross cannot be isolated from the broader biblical promise of God’s restoration of creation. Equally important is Isaiah’s vision of a renewed world, a creation in which justice, righteousness, and peace flourish under God’s reign. For Wright, the resurrection of Jesus announces the beginning of that promised new creation. The Christian hope, therefore, is not simply an escape from the present world, but the ultimate renewal of God’s good creation. Personal Stories: Mounting Up with Wings Like Eagles Amid the theological insights and biblical exposition, Wright shared several personal stories, offering the audience a glimpse into how the words of Isaiah have shaped not only his scholarship but also his spiritual imagination. One story centered on the beloved passage from Isaiah 40:31, in which the prophet declares that those who wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength and mount up with wings like eagles. Wright recalled preaching on Isaiah many years earlier and drew an amusing comparison to the long-running British radio program Desert Island Discs , in which notable guests select the recordings they would take with them if stranded on a deserted island. “I’ve sometimes said I have a set of desert island texts,” Wright explained, suggesting that certain biblical passages remain especially meaningful throughout one’s life. Near the top of his list, he said, is the closing portion of Isaiah 40, with its magnificent image of soaring eagles. The passage, he suggested, is more than a favorite theological text. It is part of his personal testimony, a biblical promise that has accompanied him through the years. A second story brought the imagery of Isaiah into an unexpected encounter with the natural world. While completing the final proofreading of Into the Heart of Isaiah , Wright and his wife, Maggie, were staying at their home in Scotland. Wright was alone in a room, carefully reviewing the text, when something outside caught his attention. “Out of the corner of my eye, I saw something,” he recalled. “At first, I thought it was somebody’s dog that had come into our front garden.” Noted Biblical archeologist, Dr. Steven Collins, listening to Mark Lanier interview Dr. NT Wright at Lanier Library. content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .

title: In the shadow of western stars: Grover Lewis, Larry McMurtry, and the triumph of words
summary: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star, the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of […]  The post  In the shadow of western stars: Grover Lewis, Larry McMurtry, and the triumph of words  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. summary: By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. content: By Charles Gardner — We used to be regular viewers of the The Great British Bake-Off TV series, now being screened on Channel 4, celebrating the efforts of amateur contestants in the kitchen. My wife is qualified in home economics and once, in her far-off student days, helped Mary Berry out over the weekend. I too like to lend a hand with my cooking skills. So when, the other day, we were intrigued to see how new presenter Nigella Lawson was doing on the show, we switched it on – and were truly appalled at the foul language spewing out of the mouths of at least two contestants. Taking the name of the Lord Jesus Christ in vain, they loudly expressed their frustration (rather than praise) at things going wrong with their concoctions in front of more than seven million viewers. We switched it off, vowing to complain in the strongest possible terms, which I have since done. And though it’s hard to be surprised at the language regularly heard on television programmes these days, I was shocked to the core by Channel 4’s response, basically saying that this particularly offensive blasphemy doesn’t come under the category of “strong language”. Really? It’s surely the worst of them all. “We are sorry to hear you were offended by some of the language used within the programme,” they wrote. “Whilst we do appreciate that you find the use of such phrases or words unacceptable, we are not obliged under the Ofcom code to obscure them, nor do they fall under the category for strong language. We therefore have no obligation to bleep them either pre- or post-watershed.” I had suggested that they could at least have edited them out, adding that they were being very hypocritical as they wouldn’t have allowed swearing in the name of Mohammed, a point which they ignored. Have we sunk so low in our nation that there is nothing left that is sacred, except woke left-wing ideology and appeasement of those who hate the God of Israel and his Son Jesus, our Lord? But we have forsaken the God who brought peace and prosperity to Britain, and who saved us from Nazi invasion, for the idols of food and celebrity. Shame on us! Is it not time the Christian world woke up and stood against this flood of filth in our midst, which will sweep us away into the oblivion of a third-rate country if we do not act soon. Where has the ‘land of hope and glory’ gone? The ‘mother of the free’ we sing about at the Proms, calling on the God ‘who made thee mighty’ to ‘make thee mightier yet’? The Apostle Paul was surely prophesying the decline and fall of the Roman Empire in his letter to the early Christians in Rome (a mixture of Jews and Gentiles), when he wrote: “The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness, since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them. For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities – his eternal power and divine nature – have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that men are without excuse.” (Romans 1:18-20) The post Offended by foul language on food show first appeared on God Reports .

title: Two truck tires and a white dove taught me to trust God
summary: By Mike Shreve — Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. Shortly after encountering […]  The post  Two truck tires and a white dove taught me to trust God  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Mike Shreve — Tent meeting in the 80s Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering Jesus and being delivered, along with another brother in the Lord, I began hitchhiking around the country, preaching the Gospel on street corners and college campuses. That developed through the years into ministry in churches, auditoriums, conferences, and tent crusades. Supernatural provision and divine intervention has always carried me, through every phase of this five-and-a-half-decade-long adventure. However, the following story is a classic. For about 25 years I carried big Gospel tents around the country. At the time of this “miracle,” I was transporting a 60’ x 90’ tent from one city to the next in an old, dilapidated bus that kept introducing new challenges to our amateur mechanic skills (putting it mildly). One day, on our way to Tampa, Florida—unfortunately—we hit a large pothole in the road that put a serious dent in the rear left rim on which a large truck tire was mounted. From that point, the inner tube would not retain air, making it necessary to stop every thirty miles or so to fill it up again . . . and again . . . and again . . . making the trip painfully slow. Adding to the problem, the other rear tire was bald, and we had no spare (couldn’t afford one). So, a flat would have brought us to a complete standstill. Sometimes, I think back on those days (when our zeal for the Kingdom outran any wisdom we might have possessed), and I marvel at the many times God took care of us anyway (like the loving heavenly Father that He is). Thousands of pounds of equipment were packed into that groaning, creaking, rusty, decrepit bus — heavy canvas tent sections, metal poles, stakes, platform, and 300 chairs—and only a few days allowed in between cities for transit and setup. No, we really could not afford any setbacks. And yes, a lot of “faith prayers” were uttered during every trip (or were they “presumptive proclamations”—not sure—maybe a mix of the two). An old split rim tire mounted on an old bus Once we got to Tampa, attempting to be frugal, I visited the junkyards hoping to find a used replacement rim. As if they had conspired to dissuade me, every junkyard owner/manager shot down my hopes with a similar assessment, “Fella, you won’t find one of them old split-rims anywhere. They’re dangerous. When you try to mount a tire on one, they can snap open and injure somebody real bad, cutting off a hand, even killing a person. We melted ‘em all down as scrap metal.” (Go ahead, look them up online—they were even called “widow-makers.”) It was the same story everywhere I went. Nobody could help. Then three weeks passed and we had to pack the bus and head to our next location—Bessemer City, North Carolina. It was a college-level, biblically-sound course on developing long-suffering and patience: stopping every thirty miles or so to air up that unpredictable tire, pleading with God to somehow supernaturally assist us in our journey by making sure none of the tires blew. Somehow, we made it—around 600 miles—stopping about 25 times. Then an incredible miracle happened! God did it and I still feel awestruck, just writing about it. As we turned into the fairgrounds area, right in the middle of the entrance were two brand new, neatly-stacked truck tires (unclaimed), exactly the size we used on the bus—mounted (you guessed it!) on the very same split rims our bus required.
